# VibeRaven

> VibeRaven is the local Studio and production-skill layer for AI-built apps.

Default command:

```bash
npx -y viberaven
```

Use the Studio cockpit for agentic chat, provider context, MCP status, release/version context, release diffs, terminal output, and access-mode control. Treat `installed` and `connected/ready` as different states for Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, and other coding CLIs; test the connection before real chat control.

Production skills help agents separate repo-code fixes from provider-human actions. Use Studio-visible context, MCP-backed provider evidence when available, relevant local tests/builds, and release/version evidence before claiming launch readiness.

Access modes matter:

- `ask`: require explicit approval behavior where supported.
- `approve`: allow normal repo edits while avoiding risky or destructive changes without explanation.
- `full`: pass full-access flags to supported CLIs and tell the connected agent that full local-project access is enabled.

Install agent rules into this repo or any repo:

```bash
npx -y viberaven init --agents all
npx -y viberaven doctor --agents
```

## Legacy scan / gate compatibility

Older VibeRaven docs may mention agent-mode scans, gate results, PRP resources, and scan-derived `nextActions`. Treat those as compatibility context, not the default public product surface. Prefer the Studio command above unless the user intentionally asks for the older scan/gate path.

- Legacy scan command: `npx -y viberaven --agent-mode`
